_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Do not be afraid, little flock.
It is the Father's good pleasure to give us the kingdom.
Keep your lamps lit and your robes ready, like servants watching for the door.
We are waiting, and our lamps are burning.
By faith Abraham set out, not knowing the way, looking for a city God would build.
We are strangers here, walking toward home.
Come, you watchers, and worship.
Our treasure is in heaven; here our hearts will be. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Picture a household late at night, lamps trimmed and burning, everyone dressed and listening for the master's knock at the door.
Do not be afraid, little flock.
That is the posture Jesus asks of us — not anxious, but ready, hearts set on the treasure no thief can reach.
Do not be afraid, little flock.
For it is the Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom; sell what binds you, and travel light.
Do not be afraid, little flock.
By faith we are walking like Abraham toward a city we have not yet seen. Keep the lamp burning; the One we wait for is faithful.
Do not be afraid, little flock. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Keep your lamps lit and watch for the door.
Do not be afraid, little flock.
Your treasure is in heaven; let your heart go there.
Do not be afraid, little flock.
Like Abraham, we walk toward a city unseen.
Do not be afraid, little flock.
Come, you watchers, and worship.
Do not be afraid, little flock. Amen.
